declarations.docstring: The duality endofunctor on the core of finitely generated modules.
The double-dual endofunctor of finitely generated modules.
An isomorphism from the identity to double dualization on finitely generated modules.
A linear equivalence between a finite free module and its double dual.
Applying the dual map twice is compatible with evaluation.
The linear automorphism defined by a functional vanishing at a chosen vector.
The value of a transvection on a vector.
An automorphism-invariant map to the dual is zero when the field has a suitable element.
An automorphism-invariant map to the dual vanishes in finite dimension at least three.
In finite dimension at least three, two vectors admit a common nonzero annihilating functional.
Extracts an algebra element from an endomorphism of scalar restriction.
Extracting the element associated with a scalar endomorphism returns that scalar.
The ring equivalence between endomorphisms of scalar restriction and the algebra.
The functor restricting scalars along an algebra structure.
Turns an algebra element into a natural endomorphism of scalar restriction.
A scalar-restriction endomorphism acts as multiplication by its extracted element.
A natural family of endomorphisms is multiplication by its value on one.
Successive scalar actions agree with multiplication of the scalars.
Extracts a ring element from an endomorphism of the identity module functor.
Extracting the central element associated with a central scalar endomorphism returns that element.
The element extracted from an identity-functor endomorphism is central.
The ring equivalence between identity-functor endomorphisms and the center.
An identity-functor endomorphism acts by its extracted ring element.
The value at one of a natural module endomorphism commutes with every ring element.
A natural module endomorphism is multiplication by its value at one.
Turns a central ring element into an endomorphism of the identity module functor.
A module is finite-dimensional exactly when it is linearly equivalent to its double dual.
A module is finite-dimensional exactly when it is linearly equivalent to its dual.
An automorphism-invariant map to the dual is not bijective when the field has a suitable element.
An automorphism-invariant map to the dual is not bijective in finite dimension at least three.
There is no isomorphism from the identity to the duality functor on finitely generated modules.
